site.name: CSS & JS Minifier
site.description: Minify CSS and JavaScript inside VS Code with one command. Install guide, quick start, shortcuts, settings and help. Runs locally and offline.

hero.badge: VS Code extension · Works offline · MIT licensed
hero.title: Make your CSS and JavaScript smaller with one command.
hero.lede: Install it, open a CSS or JavaScript file, and press Ctrl+Alt+M (Control+Option+M on a Mac). Your file gets smaller, you see how many bytes you saved, and nothing leaves your computer.

features.title: Install it
features.text: Search for the extension in the VS Code Extensions view and click Install, or run the command above in a terminal. It takes about a minute.

features.title: Open a CSS or JavaScript file
features.text: Open any .css or .js file you already have. No project setup, no config file.

features.title: Run the command
features.text: Press Ctrl+Alt+M (Control+Option+M on a Mac), or right-click and choose Minify this File. A message shows the size before and after.

features.title: Your code never leaves your machine
features.text: CSS goes through LightningCSS and JavaScript through oxc-minify, two native Rust engines that run locally. No account, no API key, no network.

features.title: Overwrite, save a .min copy, or minify on save
features.text: Keep your original and write style.min.css next to it, or turn on minify on save. Undo works like any other edit.

features.title: English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Japanese and Chinese
features.text: The extension follows your VS Code display language.

collections.label: Docs
collections.lede: Install the extension, use it, and get help. The pages for contributors are at the end.
